title.zh: 有理等离子体色散计算

summary: Evaluate a declared simple-pole rational approximation while preserving the evaluation-point shape.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to named scientific outputs.
identity.definition: Z_J(z)=sum b_j/(z-c_j), complex128 evaluation; no hidden Z-table choice or scientific-domain extrapolation.
identity.model: Nonrelativistic Gaussian species; explicit finite-harmonic/rational approximation when applicable.
identity.geometry: Homogeneous plasma with background field along z; k=(kx,0,kz) where applicable.
identity.coordinates: Explicit ES dimensionless normalization or EM SI; complex frequency follows exp(-i omega t).
identity.boundary: Periodic/infinite homogeneous plane-wave response; finite numerical harmonic/pole representation explicitly declared.
assumptions: A numerical spectrum is not automatically a physically certified mode.

inputs.name: bzj
inputs.constraints: Finite and representable in the declared numeric type.

inputs.name: czj
inputs.constraints: Finite and representable in the declared numeric type.

inputs.name: z
inputs.constraints: Finite and representable in the declared numeric type.

outputs.name: ZJ
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable in the declared numeric type.

preconditions: Constituent inputs finite and representable in declared numeric ports.
supported: Finite aligned pole/residue arrays and finite z away from declared poles.
excluded: Evaluation at a rational pole is singular.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for empty/misaligned/nonfinite poles, residues or points; exact evaluation at a rational pole raises ZeroDivisionError.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Python/dependency errors propagate; this operator launches no native process and has no native execution receipt.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: FloatingPointError for nonfinite rational output; no iterative solver or approximation-domain certification.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No successful result is returned if this operation raises; no partial scientific return is promised.

example.description: Evaluate one finite simple-pole rational term at a complex argument.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic.pdrk.rational import jpole_evaluate
r = jpole_evaluate([-1], [-1j], 1+1j)
assert np.isclose(r['ZJ'], -1/(1+2j))
example.expected: PASS: .venv/bin/python completed; ZJ equals -1/(1+2j) for the one-pole fixture. This fixture does not certify Maxwellian approximation accuracy.
